summary: 62-year-old woman on day 5 after right hemicolectomy: sudden dyspnoea and right pleuritic chest pain, HR 118, RR 26, SpO₂ 91 %, BP 112/70 — Wells PE 7 (likely).

inputs.hpi: Day 5 after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for caecal cancer. Sudden breathlessness this morning with sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing in. No cough, no haemoptysis. Mobilising slowly. Enoxaparin prophylaxis started day 1.

exam.general: Breathless at rest. HR 118, RR 26, SpO2 91% on air, BP 112/70, T 37.6°C.
exam.respiratory: Chest clear, no pleural rub. No focal signs.
exam.abdomen: Port sites clean, abdomen soft, appropriately tender.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected pulmonary embolism (post-operative)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected post-operative pulmonary embolism, Wells PE 7 (likely): immediate CTPA, interim therapeutic anticoagulation if CTPA is delayed and bleeding risk acceptable (day 5 after bowel resection — senior decision).

mustNotMiss.note: Post-operative tachycardia and hypoxia: leak and chest infection are the alternatives.

mustInclude.note: Interim therapeutic anticoagulation if CTPA is delayed, weighed against post-operative bleeding risk.

mustExclude.note: Wells PE >4 (likely): CTPA directly, interim anticoagulation if delayed; ≤4: D-dimer first. A D-dimer gate or a Wells ≥2 threshold (the DVT cut-off) does not follow NICE NG158, and D-dimer is uninformative after surgery.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 — Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: DVT: two-level Wells; likely (≥2) → proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation and D-dimer if delayed); unlikely → D-dimer. PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) → CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely (≤4) → D-dimer; PERC may be used when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing (NG158). London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: 2019 ESC guidelines — acute pulmonary embolism
guideline.section: Suspected PE without haemodynamic instability: clinical probability (Wells/Geneva), D-dimer only when probability is not high, CTPA; anticoagulation started while awaiting results in high/intermediate probability
guideline.citation: Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J. 2020;41:543–603.

guideline.name: Wells PE score (two-level)
guideline.section: Clinical signs of DVT 3; PE most likely diagnosis 3; HR >100 1.5; immobilisation ≥3 days or surgery within 4 weeks 1.5; previous VTE 1.5; haemoptysis 1; malignancy 1; >4 = PE likely
guideline.citation: Wells PS, Anderson DR, Rodger M, et al. Derivation of a simple clinical model to categorize patients probability of pulmonary embolism. Thromb Haemost. 2000;83:416–20.

guideline.name: YEARS algorithm for suspected PE
guideline.section: Three items (clinical signs of DVT, haemoptysis, PE most likely diagnosis) with D-dimer thresholds of 1000 ng/mL (no items) or 500 ng/mL (≥1 item)
guideline.citation: van der Hulle T, Cheung WY, Kooij S, et al. Simplified diagnostic management of suspected pulmonary embolism (the YEARS study): a prospective, multicentre, cohort study. Lancet. 2017;390:289–97.

rationale: Base PE case: post-operative, Wells PE 7 (HR >100 1.5, surgery within 4 weeks 1.5, malignancy 1, PE most likely 3), hypoxic. PERC does not apply (age, HR, SpO₂, surgery); YEARS would apply a 500 ng/mL threshold but NICE sends Wells-likely patients straight to CTPA. Tests ranking, hypoxia alarm, CTPA and the D-dimer gate.
